stories.title: Portuguese Company Turns Cork Wood into Limitless Material, Even to Insulate Spacecraft
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: A 150-year-old Portuguese company that has made wine corks since the days of the monarchy has found remarkable new uses for cork. Because cork oak bark can be harvested again and again without harming the tree, it's one of the most renewable materials on Earth. The company has turned it into insulation strong and light enough to protect spacecraft from extreme heat. It's a lovely example of an old, sustainable craft finding a cutting-edge new purpose. Nothing about it required cutting down a single tree.
stories.why_good: A real, already-operating company turning a renewable natural material into high-tech, planet-friendly products.

stories.title: Teens Set World Record for Most Sports Balls Recycled in One Day, Diverting 2,675 Pounds from Landfills
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: A group of teen environmentalists in California set out to break a Guinness World Record for recycling sports balls, and they pulled it off. In one day, they collected around 22,000 old racquet sport balls weighing over 2,675 pounds, keeping all of it out of landfills. The balls will be broken down and turned into new materials instead of sitting in the trash for years. It's a fun reminder that young people are finding creative ways to tackle waste, one bouncy ball at a time.
stories.why_good: An actual completed event (a world record achieved) that kept real waste out of landfills, led by young people, with zero political content.
